text:
A10 done, commit 2aabf54. `./gradlew assembleDebug lint test` eventually
green: 0 lint errors, same 23 pre-existing warnings. 100 tests / 21
suites, 0 failures on the confirmed-clean run.

Real bug found via an unplanned live-server check: SessionDto.deviceLabel
was non-nullable but the real dev server (:8723) returns device_label:
null for sessions from clients that never sent a label (curl, etc).
Fixed to String? + a UI fallback ("Unknown device") + a regression test.
Worth internalizing: every ticket so far that's the FIRST to actually
decode a given endpoint's real response (A3's DTOs generally, now A10 for
/account/sessions) has found at least one nullability mismatch against
live data that unit tests with hand-written JSON fixtures didn't catch,
since the fixtures were written from the Wire Contract's *documented*
shape, not from what the server actually emits in edge cases. If A9 is
the first ticket to decode GET /lists/{id}/members or invite responses
for real, expect the same category of surprise there - a live curl check
before writing the DTOs, not just after, might catch it earlier next
time.

Infra note - encountered and want to flag rather than let repeat silently:
this build hit two DIFFERENT flaky test failures on consecutive full-suite
runs today ("Dispatchers.Main is used concurrently with setting it" and
UncompletedCoroutinesError, both in kotlinx-coroutines-test's
TestMainDispatcher, in DIFFERENT pre-existing test files neither touched
by this ticket - AddItemDialogTest and ItemFormViewModelTest, both from
A8). Both vanished on rerun with zero code changes. Correlated with
sustained heavy Gradle activity (load average 2.7-3.3 at the time, after
many consecutive full builds during this ticket's debugging). Tried
Test.maxParallelForks=1 as a fix; it did NOT resolve it (recurred anyway)
so that change was reverted rather than left in as unproven complexity.
Best working theory: Robolectric's internal per-test thread-pooled
execution (visible in the stack traces via Sandbox.runOnMainThread)
interacting with kotlinx-coroutines-test's process-global Dispatchers.Main
under real scheduling jitter, not a logic bug. If this recurs in A9 (the
last remaining Android ticket) or beyond, don't chase it as a regression
in whatever code was just written first - check `git diff` shows nothing
suspicious in the failing (usually unrelated) test file, then just rerun.
If it becomes frequent enough to slow work down, the next real lever
(untried) is isolating Robolectric-heavy suites into their own Gradle Test
task/JVM rather than tuning fork counts.

Design carried forward for A9: ThemePreferenceStore's pattern (separate
DataStore + Hilt qualifier annotation, because a second unqualified
DataStore<Preferences> binding collides with ServerConfig's) is the
template for any future ticket needing its own small persisted
client-only setting.
